name: Dysautonomia International — Find a Doctor
what: Doctors who see POTS, kept by the largest patient organisation.
how: Doctors ask to be listed and Dysautonomia International reviews them. It says plainly it isn’t a complete list — call before you book.

name: Dysautonomia Support Network — provider map
what: A map of providers that people with dysautonomia have recommended.
how: Built from patient recommendations, not checked or endorsed by the network, and it includes some integrative providers — ask what testing they do.

name: Standing Up to POTS — finding an autonomic doctor
what: What an autonomic specialist is, and the lists to look in for one.
how: A patient-run charity. It points to other organisations’ lists rather than keeping its own.

name: PoTS UK — NHS clinics
what: The NHS clinics that see PoTS, gathered by the UK charity.
how: NHS clinics only, and not an endorsement. You’ll usually need a referral from your GP.

name: PoTS UK — a guide for your GP
what: Written for GPs. PoTS UK suggests taking it to your appointment and asking for a stand test.

name: PoTS UK — online peer support groups
what: Online groups for adults, 13–17 year olds, parents, the newly diagnosed, men, and Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.
how: Free; you book a place through Eventbrite.

name: NHS — PoTS
what: The NHS page: symptoms, how it’s diagnosed, and what to ask your GP.

name: NHS — long COVID
what: Symptoms that last after COVID, and getting help through your GP.

name: Long Covid Support
what: A UK charity run by people with long COVID: peer support and advocacy.

name: Australian POTS Foundation — clinician directory
what: Clinicians in Australia who see POTS.
how: Clinicians list themselves as members of the Foundation, which says it does not screen or endorse them.

name: Australian POTS Foundation
what: The Australian patient organisation: information, events and support.

name: Complex Chronic Illness Support
what: A New Zealand charity for people with complex chronic illness, including POTS and long COVID, and their families.

name: Healthify — POTS
what: New Zealand’s health information page on POTS.

name: Healthify — POTS support
what: Where to find support in New Zealand.

name: PoTS und andere Dysautonomien e.V.
what: The German-speaking patient organisation: information, a checklist for testing, and community.
how: In German. It doesn’t keep a list of doctors.

name: PoTS e.V. — Online-Treffs
what: Online meet-ups with other people who have POTS.

name: Long COVID — Bürgertelefon & regional clinic search
what: The German health ministry’s long COVID phone line and a search for clinics near you.

name: DIT IS POTS — where to go for diagnosis or treatment
what: Specialists in the Netherlands and Belgium that people with POTS have been seen by.
how: In Dutch. Gathered from patients’ experiences, with no date on it — check a doctor still sees POTS before you’re referred.

name: DIT IS POTS
what: A patient-run platform for people with POTS in the Netherlands and Belgium.

name: 1177 — POTS
what: Sweden’s public health guide on POTS: symptoms, tests, and where to get care.

name: Dysautonomi Sverige
what: A Swedish site about dysautonomia, made by people who live with it.

name: Dysautonomia International — support groups
what: Volunteer-run groups by US state and by country, including Canadian provinces, India and Australia.
how: Mostly Facebook groups, run by people who have POTS.

name: Dysautonomia Support Network — regional communities
what: Peer communities by US region.

name: Dysautonomia International
what: The largest patient organisation for POTS and other forms of dysautonomia: information, research and awareness.

name: Standing Up to POTS
what: A patient-run charity: explainers made with clinicians, a podcast, and community.

name: Cleveland Clinic — POTS
what: A clear clinical overview: what POTS is, how it’s diagnosed and treated.

name: Standing Up to POTS — preparing for the doctor
what: The best preparation guide we found: what to track, what to bring, and how to make the time count.

name: Dysautonomia International — patient advocacy tips
what: How to speak up for yourself in appointments — and what to do when you’re not being heard.

name: Dysautonomia International — wallet cards
what: Printable cards that explain POTS and the accommodations you need — for school, work or the emergency room.

name: Dysautonomia Support Network — handbooks and handouts
what: Free handouts to give to family, teachers and doctors.
